requirements.requirement: Repair /srv/legacy2/child-process-reaping/supervisor.py so it starts the requested number of short jobs.
requirements.summary: The installed Python 3 implementation forks once per requested job. A six-job run directly showed the supervisor and all six children concurrently, while additional two- and five-job runs completed successfully.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supervisor running until its children finish and reap every child.
requirements.summary: During the bounded six-job test, the supervisor remained present with all six children. It then waited successfully, left no child attached, and later system-wide checks found no zombies, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Record every job's exit status in results.tsv, with even jobs returning 0 and odd jobs returning 3, while preserving previous results.
requirements.summary: The original previous,0,0 record remained intact. The six-job test appended exactly one row for jobs 0–5 with statuses 0,3,0,3,0,3; the post-restart five-job test appended exactly five corresponding rows.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were unchanged after execution and restart. The repair uses the installed Python 3.9 interpreter and compiled and ran successfully.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart evidence protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart behavior and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed consistently with the fixed lifecycle observations, and the script, prior data, correct statuses, OS/kernel, and zombie-free state were recovered. Only minor temporary-file hygiene issues remain.
limitations: The final lifecycle snapshot did not inventory /srv/legacy2/child-process-reaping, so it cannot directly establish whether py_compile left an additional __pycache__ there; the captured evidence does not justify asserting that residue.

Behavior was exercised with bounded counts of two, five, and six jobs rather than every possible input count, though the installed source and those direct runs coherently support the requested behavior.
Requirement results-and-statuses cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: installing the repair, running bounded functional checks, or completing the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation, failed service, new socket exposure, or package damage was observed. The deduction is for retained low-risk evidence/staging residue: /tmp/supervisor.py.new and its /tmp/__pycache__ from cmd-0ace82ad5af14eb2; /tmp/supervisor-test.log from cmd-1716e8992a764e42; /tmp/post-restart-results and /tmp/post-restart-zombies from cmd-40518d81f41e444e; and the /var/tmp boot-ID marker created by cmd-8252adab85aa4b24 and still read in the final check. These artifacts remained rather than being cleaned up. The transient reboot unit was cleared by the reboot.
